newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates rise in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates rise in brisk trade.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate edged up to 9.8 percent from 9.1 on Friday as demand grew and some lenders raised their interest rates, dealers said.
They said fresh loans, which accounted for all the trading on the Zagreb money market, totalled 32.1 million kuna against Thursday's 12 million.
Demand totalling 50 million kuna overshot supply by 18 million, as some lenders asked for loans to be repaid. The insurers' money rate rose to nine percent from eight.
Call money placements made by state bank HBOR at 12 pct raised the overall call money rate to 9.5 pct from 9.0 pct.
Thursday's overnight trade was 22.6 million kuna.
The central bank's midrates for the weekend and Monday firmed to 5,3700 kuna to the dollar and 3,5662 to the German mark. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
